### C30 — 1 Thess. 2:13–16 not a post-70 interpolation (Weima’s defense)
**Locus:** cache L280–L326
**Quote:** "only one passage has attracted significant support as a later interpolation: 2:13–16" … Pearson’s theological, historical, form-critical arguments + Schmidt’s linguistic argument "not as compelling as their proponents claim" … "universal textual support" in every extant MS
**Claim:** Weima rejects Pearson/Schmidt interpolation theory:
- **Theological:** Rom. 9–11 also has severe Jewish judgments; 2:14–16 targets limited group (or geographical "Judeans"); εἰς τέλος as "until the end" may leave room for future salvation; 1 Cor. 2:8 "rulers" need not contradict Jewish involvement.
- **Historical:** aorist ἔφθασεν is past but need not mean 70 destruction—other pre-50 calamities or gospel-rejection as wrath; Judean Christian suffering attested pre-70 (Paul’s own persecution; Agrippa I; late-40s/early-50s Zealot pressure).
- **Form-critical:** second thanksgiving not anomalous (cf. 2 Thess. 2:13–14); 2:13 may not be formal thanksgiving; Paul adapts forms; 2:13–16 continues 1:5–10 pattern (mission → response); "and because of this" links to 2:1–12; emphatic "we" at 2:17 works better with 2:13–16 present.
- **Linguistic:** Pauline variation + possible traditional material; parallels for καί / embedding / word order; "and because of this" also in 2 Thess. 2:11.
- **Textual:** no floating location unlike Rom. 16:25–27 or 1 Cor. 14:34–35.
**Target pages:** `1-thessalonians`, `paul-apostle`, `weima-1-2-thessalonians-becnt`, `jeffrey-weima`, Miscellaneous (1 Thess 2:13–16 interpolation debate — no dedicated controversy slug)

### C32 — Four anti-authenticity arguments and Weima’s rebuttals
**Locus:** cache L336–L386
**Quote:** "Four major arguments… (1) the colder, authoritarian tone… (2) the authenticating comment of 3:17… (3) the eschatological differences… (4) the literary dependence"
**Claim:** Weima (with Marshall, Wanamaker, Still, Malherbe, Foster) finds each argument weak:
1. **Tone:** "myth of the cold tone" (Marshall); "we ought to give thanks" intensifies affection; high "brothers" rate; firmer tone fits crisis (false prophecy; idle rebellion)—cf. 1 Cor. 4:21; Gal. 4:19–20.
2. **3:17 autograph:** not unique emphatic autograph; sensible if forged letter feared (2:2); may stress Paul’s *authority* re. idlers (3:14) more than authenticity; author knows only 1 Thess. among Pauline corpus (no autograph note there).
3. **Eschatology:** alleged thief-without-warning vs. preceding signs misreads 1 Thess. 5—unbelievers surprised; believers "know well," are sons of light, not overtaken; both letters urge ready/steady lives and election-comfort; differences minor, situation-driven (false "day has come").
4. **Literary dependence (Wrede/Trilling):** subjectivity (creativity vs expected reuse to same church/topics); paradox (too similar *and* too different); illogic of forger knowing only 1 Thess. and nothing of later Paul (Fee).
**Cumulative-force logic rejected:** stacking weak arguments does not yield a strong case (Jewett, Wanamaker).
**Target pages:** `2-thessalonians-authorship`, `2-thessalonians`, `1-thessalonians`, `parousia-1-thess-4`, `restrainer-2-thess-2`, `paul-apostle`, `jeffrey-weima`, `weima-1-2-thessalonians-becnt`
